reasoning_summary: Round 1 uses the baseline assessment only, since there is no prior HPO feedback. The baseline indicates overfitting (train-CV R² gap 0.219, CV R² below threshold). With a small training set (n_train=153) and only 1 feature, I biased the grid toward stronger regularization and a compact search: larger n_neighbors values are emphasized to smooth predictions, while still retaining a few smaller values to avoid excessive underfitting. I included only valid KNeighborsRegressor settings from the allowed parameter list and kept the total combinations well below the 120-candidate limit.
search_strategy: Compact regularization-focused grid centered on moderate-to-larger neighborhood sizes, with both weighting schemes and valid distance metrics/norms to address baseline overfitting without creating an unnecessarily large search space.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Increasing n_neighbors relative to very local fits should reduce variance and shrink the train-CV gap; uniform weighting may further regularize compared with distance weighting.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: There is some risk that larger neighborhoods may oversmooth signal, but inclusion of moderate neighbor counts and both weighting options preserves flexibility.
computational_cost_estimate: Low; 9 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 108 candidates, within the 120 maximum.
warnings: Some parameter combinations are redundant because metric='euclidean' corresponds to p=2 and metric='manhattan' corresponds to p=1; they are retained to stay within the allowed schema and candidate budget.
Because there is only 1 feature, performance gains may be limited by representation rather than hyperparameters alone.
If this grid shifts too far toward underfitting, the next round should reintroduce smaller n_neighbors more aggressively.
